sources.title: Sub-optimality of Marton's Inner Bound for the Two-Receiver Broadcast Channel

declaredTheoremScope.name: Constraint removal
declaredTheoremScope.summary: For a finite broadcast channel T and a finite concave f upper-bounding the fixed-input Marton functional, a prescribed p* and two-letter witness whose two coordinate marginals average to p* and whose value is strictly greater than 2 f(p*) imply existence of a finite unconstrained channel T' with M(T' tensor 2)>2M(T').

declaredTheoremScope.name: Sub-optimality of Marton's inner bound
declaredTheoremScope.summary: There exists a finite two-receiver discrete memoryless broadcast channel T tilde with M(T tilde tensor 2)>2M(T tilde), so its complete one-letter Marton region is strictly contained in its capacity region.

inputAlphabetScope.binaryInputStatus: not proved; the paper says counterexamples appear to require nonbinary input and concludes that binary-input tightness remains open

sources.title: Counterexamples to the Markovity Conjecture for the Two-Receiver Broadcast Channel

declaredTheoremScope.name: Markov class cardinality reduction
declaredTheoremScope.summary: For finite input alphabet size m, every finite-alphabet U-X-V law has a same-input-marginal Markov replacement with |U'|,|V'| at most m and no smaller G_alpha value; consequently the literal Markov-class supremum is attained.

declaredTheoremScope.name: Markov/rectangular equivalence
declaredTheoremScope.summary: For a finite-input channel with strictly positive receiver marginals and no duplicate pair of receiver-marginal rows, fixed potential c, and 0<alpha<1, a Markov unrestricted global optimizer exists if and only if some unrestricted global optimizer is a deterministic rectangular encoder.
